summary.text: A 35-year-old gravida 2, para 0 mother had a penicillin allergy, GBS-positive vaginal swabs, normal amniocentesis chromosomal and SNP microarray results and no family history of HLH, early neonatal deaths or known consanguinity. After labor induction with oxytocin, a female neonate weighing 3,480 g with Apgar scores of 9, 10 and 10 was delivered by cesarean section on May 6, with an unremarkable delivery-room examination without hepatosplenomegaly.

Approximately 3 h after birth the neonate developed abdominal distension and fever (38 °C) and was transferred to the NICU. Examination showed lethargy, widespread petechiae and ecchymoses, pallor, tachypnea, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly and absent bowel sounds. Laboratory studies showed thrombocytopenia (30 × 10^(9)/L), fibrinogen 0.77 g/L, D-dimer 26,074 μg/L, triglycerides 3.78 mmol/L, ferritin >40,000 μg/L, lactate 9.7 mmol/L and a metabolic acidosis; CRP was 5.1 mg/L. Cultures, plasma mNGS and metabolic screening were negative; sIL-2R, NK-cell cytotoxicity and TORCH studies were not obtained.

Echocardiography six hours after NICU admission showed left ventricular dysfunction (EF 0.47), enlarged left atrium and ventricle, a patent ductus arteriosus with a predominantly right-to-left bidirectional shunt and pulmonary hypertension. By 9 h post-admission saturation had dropped to 80%, requiring endotracheal intubation and PC-SIMV ventilation; radiography showed pulmonary exudates progressing to pulmonary hemorrhage, with gastrointestinal bleeding and worsening DIC. Nitric oxide, vasopressors and milrinone were given and the family declined ECMO.

The infant died on day 5 of life with multiorgan failure. Post-mortem whole-exome sequencing identified compound heterozygous PRF1 variants (c.1131C>A inherited from the father and c.65delC from the mother), confirming FHL2; induction therapy and HSCT were precluded by the fulminant course. The family received genetic counselling.

caption_evidence.quote:
FIGURE 1
Sanger sequencing chromatograms showing compound heterozygous mutations in the PRF1 gene in the index case and parents. The top three panels (A–C) show sequencing results for the PRF1 c.1131C>A (p.Cys377Ter) nonsense mutation. (A) Index case: heterozygous C>A transition at nucleotide position c.1131 (red arrow). (B) Father: heterozygous for the same C>A mutation. (C) Mother: wild-type sequence (CC). The bottom three panels (D–F) display the PRF1 c.65delC (p.Pro22Argfs*29) frameshift mutation. (D) Index case: heterozygous deletion of cytosine at position c.65 (red arrow). (E) Father: wild-type sequence. (F) Mother: heterozygous deletion of cytosine. These chromatograms confirm that the index case carries compound heterozygous mutations in PRF1, consistent with autosomal recessive familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis type 2 (FHL2). Red arrows indicate the exact mutation sites.
